ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners holding 25% or more ultimate beneficial ownership, directors, attorneys-in-fact, and authorized representatives against: Global Affairs Canada consolidated Canadian autonomous sanctions list; Canadian Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act sanctions lists; OFAC SDN list; UN Security Council Consolidated List; HM Treasury and EU sanctions lists for cross-border counterparties; FINTRAC politically exposed persons (PEP) data sets; and domestic public official and integrity registries. Adverse media and source-of-wealth checks are required for all PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, and cash-heavy counterparties. Screening results and related AML/CFT documentation must be retained for at least five years under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must satisfy the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11. A Quebec limited partnership must use French in its declared name or provide a French version; the English equivalent may appear alongside. Latin-script transliteration is required for any non-Latin name; the legal designation must be included in the form of either 'société en commandite' (S.E.C.) or 'Limited Partnership' (L.P.) as applicable. Names must be distinctive, not misleading, and must not falsely imply incorporation, a financial institution, a professional order, or a public authority.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal, the applicant may file a written administrative review request with the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of the rejection notice. The review must cite the file number, the statutory ground in CQLR c P-44.1, and include corrective evidence such as consents from holders of similar names, trademarks, or revised distinctive elements. If the refusal is maintained, the applicant may apply for judicial review before the Superior Court of Quebec under the Code of Civil Procedure, CQLR c C-25.01, art. 529, within a reasonable delay. A new name reservation application may be submitted immediately after the administrative review is exhausted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only when the virtual office provider supplies a physical street address in Quebec and undertakes to receive documents on behalf of the partnership. A post-office box or mail-forwarding address alone is not acceptable. The virtual address may serve as the registered office for a passive holding, trading, or scale-model distribution LP; however, actual zinc die-casting and tampo-printing operations must take place in a commercial or industrial premise lawfully permitting that activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. Estimated 10-15% probability of an unannounced physical inspection during the first operating year for a passive LP; probability rises to 25-35% if the partnership registers a Quebec industrial facility for die-casting or otherwise maintains inventory, imports/export-subject goods, or employs local staff.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c. CCQ-1991), arts. 2236-2279 (société en commandite) and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), arts. 1, 7, 27-31 (declaration of registration and legal publicity obligations).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) / Registrar of Enterprises of Quebec, Legal Publicity Service
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) filed in the Registre des entreprises du Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum share capital for a société en commandite. Contributions (cash, property, or industry/service) are freely negotiated in the private limited partnership agreement; no escrow account or capital verification is statutorily mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned general partners, constituting the governing body of [Insert LP Name], a société en commandite formed under the Civil Code of Québec, are authorized to prepare and file all documents required for registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the capital contributions subscribed by the limited partners, as stated in the limited partnership agreement, are hereby unconditionally accepted, and that the registered office of the Partnership is established at [full street address], Québec. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [General Partner Name] is appointed as managing general partner with exclusive authority to operate the zinc die-casting and tampo printing establishment, and [Nominee Name] is appointed as representative for service of legal notices. PASSED by the general partners this ___ day of __________, 20___.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Pre-registration Availability Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a prior name search in the Registre des entreprises database, verify availability against distinctive signs database of the REQ, and submit a name reservation request through the online enterprise services portal; the reservation is valid for 60 days and must be attached to the declaration of registration upon filing.
required_dossiers: Reservation request form (online)
Proposed corporate/partnership name in French or bilingual
Identity details and contact information of the general partner applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for distinctiveness or conflict, submit an amended request with an alternative name; the refusal notice may be objected to in writing to the REQ Danalyzer, and the Tribunal administratif du Québec may hear the dispute after internal review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement and Capital Contribution Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil-law notary (notaire) if an immovable or formal deed is required; otherwise private deed among partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a written limited partnership agreement defining the object (zinc alloy die-casting and tampo printing of 1:18 scale automotive replicas), capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios, management powers of the general partners, and admission rights of the limited partners; if partnership capital includes immovable property, the agreement must be notarized and published in the Land Register.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of each general and limited partner
Capital contribution schedule (cash, equipment, or material services)
Completed limited partnership agreement
Notarized deed (only when an immovable is contributed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the agreement by unanimous consent of the partners before notarization; a rectification deed or supplementary convention may be executed and filed as a modification if the initial deed is incomplete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online portal for legal publicity
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the REQ online service using a government-issued credential, complete the Déclaration d'immatriculation for a société en commandite, enter the partnership name, object, establishment address in Québec, full details of all general partners, and deliberate the declaration before a commissioner for oaths if paper filing is used; pay the applicable filing fee by credit card or direct debit.
required_dossiers: Completed declaration of registration form
Reserved name confirmation (if obtained)
Eve of tax data of general partners (full name, domicile, birth date, social insurance number if resident)
Proof of the establishment address in Québec (lease or title)
Partnership agreement extract confirming capital contributions and management authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ sends a query or refusal, respond with supplementary information through the same portal within 30 days; if the declaration is defective, withdraw it and refile an amended declaration within the prescribed delay, paying no additional fee if the correction is made before registration is closed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Québec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and Activation of Provincial Tax and Employer Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (NEQ issuance) and Revenu Québec (tax registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, the REQ issues the NEQ and publishes the partnership entry in the public registry; the general partners then apply to Revenu Québec for a QST account, GST/HST registration, source deductions and employer contributions for employees, and a videotron/administrative accounts as required. The registrations may be combined online via the 'clients' section of Revenu Québec.
required_dossiers: NEQ confirmation notice
Basis of the partnership's taxable supplies (projected revenues)
Identification of the general partner manager
Bank account details for payroll/remittance purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Revenu Québec delays account opening, file a priority notice through the customer portal, or contact the taxpayer services desk; errors in account type can be cured by filing a 'Demande de modification' online.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business License and Zoning Compliance Fit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality (Ville de Montréal / MRC) — Permis d'exploitation and Service d'urbanisme
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a municipal application for a business permit (Permis d'exploitation) and an occupancy/construction permit for the leasehold or owned industrial premises; verify that the zone allows light manufacturing (Classe de production industrielle), including die-casting and printing operations; obtain a certificate of compliance with the local by-law respecting noise, odors, and storage.
required_dossiers: Municipal application form for business permit
NEQ and REQ registration excerpt
Lease or ownership deed
Zoning and building occupancy certificate
Floor plan and description of die-casting and tampo printing equipment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If zoning is non-conforming, request a 'revision de zonage' variance or relocate to an industrial MRC zone; if the permit application is quenched, correct the missing plans and immediately re-submit to the municipal permitting office, or appeal to the municipal review committee (Comité de dérogation).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — Direction de l'autorisation et de la conformité (Section des autorisations des établissements industriels)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificat d'autorisation (CA) for the operation of an industrial establishment under section 22 of the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c. E-1.1) — covering the zinc alloy die-casting foundry and tampo printing lines

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP), Legal Assessment Directorate
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class III — Pre-operational authorization with a sectoral environmental impact study; full public EIA (BAPE) is not triggered unless non-ferrous metal melting capacity exceeds 50 tonnes per day (Schedule I of the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment). The 1:18 scale automotive model plant is expected to fall below the threshold, requiring a 'Conception environnementale' report rather than an exhaustive impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Process wastewater: zinc ≤ 5 mg/L, lead ≤ 2 mg/L, pH 6.0–9.5, and compliance with municipal sewer-use by-laws; atmospheric: total suspended particulates (TSP) ≤ 100 mg/Nm³, volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from tampo printing inks must be recovered when annual emissions exceed the regulatory threshold (Règlement sur l'assainissement de l'atmosphère, annexes K and L); hazardous residues (dross, spent flux, solvents) must be managed under the Règlement sur les matières dangereuses with a registered manifest system.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Quebec Commission for Standards, Equity, Health and Safety at Work (CNESST) registration under the Act respecting occupational health and safety; municipal fire safety certificate under the Loi sur la sécurité incendie (fire extinguishers, access, and emergency lighting); structural and floor-loading verification for the die-casting presses and storage racks; electrical wiring inspection of the die-casting machines; and a mechanical guard/heat-protection compliance report for the molten zinc furnace and tampo printing oven.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada — Business Registration Online (BRO) portal (www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/registering-your-business.html). Provincial (Quebec): Revenu Québec (www.revenuquebec.ca) — registration integrated through the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) one-stop portal; QST, source deductions and provincial accounts are administered by Revenu Québec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1: Register the LP's legal personality in Quebec with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain the 10-digit NEQ (Quebec enterprise number), filing the declaration of registration under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and the C.c.Q. fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully floating exchange rate system with unrestricted convertibility of the Canadian dollar on both current and capital accounts. There are no statutory exchange controls, no prior-approval requirements for external remittances, and no distinction between capital and current account transactions. Profit repatriation by a limited partnership is subject only to domestic income tax and Part XIII withholding tax under applicable tax treaties, not to foreign exchange authorization. Non-resident investors may freely subscribe to and withdraw capital, provided that FINTRAC reporting thresholds for wire transfers and international electronic funds transfers are met. The Bank of Canada Act and the Currency Act impose no restriction on holding, transferring, or converting foreign currency balances within or outside Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canadian exporters are not required to surrender export proceeds to the government or any authorized dealer, and there is no statutory timeline requiring conversion into CAD. Export revenue may be retained in foreign currency accounts with Canadian chartered banks. Reporting obligations are limited to FINTRAC cross-border electronic funds transfer reports for amounts equal to or exceeding CAD $10,000, and to the Canada Revenue Agency for annual taxpayer reporting. No deposit or reserve margin is required.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for ancillary settlement; Low for primary operating accounts. Under Quebecs Anti-Money Laundering Act and federal Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, any entity providing money-transfer or foreign-exchange services to residents must be registered as a money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC and maintain a permanent establishment or agent in Canada. Major offshore digital EMIs such as Wise and PayPal Canada are FINTRAC-registered; however, non-registered foreign EMIs cannot lawfully receive and settle trade payments for a Canadian-domiciled partnership. Additionally, commercial banking agreements restrict the use of PayPal for bulk B2B settlement due to reserve holds and chargeback provisions. The only viable offshore-EMI use is for payment to remote subcontractors, capped at CAD $5,000 per transaction, with each beneficiary KYC-verified. Cross-border clearing for die-cast scale automotive model imports and exports must route through the SWIFT network via a Canadian bank to preserve auditability and mitigate Bank Secrecy Act risks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is mandatory for the general partner and all limited partners holding more than 20% of the partnership interests when opening a Capital Escrow Account or when the initial aggregate funding exceeds CAD $250,000. For operational accounts below this threshold, banks permit remote account opening using video-confirmed identity verification by a designated in-branch officer or notary practising in Quebec. In all cases, original or notarized copies of the following must be produced: (1) the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) registration certificate and Declaration of Partnership, (2) the partnership agreement, (3) a resolution of the general partner authorizing the bank account, (4) personal identification for each officer or partner, and (5) a completed corporate resolution in the bank's prescribed form. The Anti-Money Laundering regulations (FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA) require identification of any beneficial owner with more than 20% of the partnership capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners controlling more than 20% interest without a Canadian banking record
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide per partner: certified passport copy, tax residence certificate from their personal jurisdiction, a notarized declaration (Form, note) describing the provenance of subscription funds, six months of bank statements from the source bank, crystallized foreign equity or bank reference letter, and a signed representation letter from each partner confirming no politically exposed person (PEP) status. If funding originates via a holding entity, provide original certificate of registry, group organizational chart, and audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trade in zinc alloy die-cast automotive replicas categorized under HS 9503 that could trigger gagged intellectual property confiscation or sanctions scoping
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present a product-binding tariff classification opinion from the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) confirming the goods do not infringe automotive OEM trademark interests and are non-defence ancillary. Supply: sample container bill of lading, purchase orders from independent distributors, letter from the manufacturer confirming die-cast scale models are not functional vehicle components, and copies of the commercial agreements showing no underlying end user of functional automotive part restrictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital escrow account receiving frequent wire transfers from non-bank third parties or online payment platforms
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce a cash-flow projection model matching contribution schedules to the LP agreement, the executed merger/acquisition contribution schedule, and source-of-funds documentation for each remitter, including bank or platform confirmation. Include an anti-money laundering internal policy manual, completed daily risk assessment for the synthetic signature, and an audited trial balance showing wire traceability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to demonstrate a tangible place of business in the province of Quebec
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit REQ Attestation of Registration for a limited partnership, retail sales permit from Revenu Québec, GST/HST confirmation from Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), and a lease agreement for a storage or office facility in Quebec with a utility tax statement. Provide corporate bank statements with 12 months of Quebec-based rent payments and a signed representation that accounting and inventory records will remain in the province.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity contributions to the Quebec Limited Partnership should be executed via SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from the parent or limited partners' bank directly to the LP's primary operating account at a Canadian chartered bank. The remitter name must exactly match the initial contribution schedule registered in the partnership agreement; any mismatch triggers FINTRAC Enhanced Due Diligence. The transaction must include clear purpose codes: for capital account funding use 'P0120' under SWIFT category 'Investment Income and Financing' (or FINTRAC code 'or-Investment'), accompanied by a detailed invoice or funding notice, and for customer deposits use 'P0135'. All transfers exceeding CAD $10,000 require the bank to file an Electronic Funds Transfer Report (EFTR) with FINTRAC within 30 days. Canada has no special licensing requirement for inbound capital, but the LP must ensure the CRA Form T2/ANZ or relevant provincial filings schedule the contribution appropriately, ensuring no Part XIII tax leakage.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for raw zinc alloy, blister package resins, tampo printing inks, and import/export of finished die-cast replicas must use SWIFT MT103 direct wire transfers for payments under USD 1,000,000. For larger wholesale transactions, Commercial Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) and irrevocable Letters of Credit (LC) issued through a participating Montreal-based bank are preferred. Each MT103 must identify source of funds with a unique beneficiary account number and instruct the beneficiary bank to provide an IMAD reference that ties to the commercial invoice; PA-03 advise and storage endorsements must be avoided. All outbound disbursements over CAD $10,000 are reportable to FINTRAC and must be filed with the CRA under the Income Tax Act reporting requirements (T-batch form). The LP must retain full remitting instruction history in ISO 20022 XML format to support transfer of proceeds and to meet the Quebec Financial Administration Act.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright foreign exchange forward contracts (deliverable forwards) against USD, EUR, JPY, and CNY
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing a liquid freely convertible currency pair with a Canadian bank counterparty
Cross-currency swaps (synthetic USD/CAD floating-to-floating or fixed-to-floating) under standard ISDA agreements
Vanilla foreign exchange options (call and put options) with maturities up to 12 months

Accumulative forward-similar structures known as forward-active options (FX averaging forwards) executed with an Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) federally regulated Schedule I bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) of the Limited Partnership under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the limited partnership's registration date in Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 400 for a partnership (CAD 200 for an individual enterprise) plus interest on outstanding fees; administrative strike-off (radiation d'office) by the REQ after three consecutive years of unfiled annual declarations; a struck-off partnership loses the right to exercise its activities in Quebec and forfeits the protections of legal publicity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return, T5013 Summary, and T5013 slips allocating income, loss, and tax credits to each partner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end (e.g., by June 30 for a December 31 fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day (minimum CAD 100) up to CAD 2,500 under subsection 162(7) of the Income Tax Act; gross-negligence penalties apply for knowingly false statements; partners may be denied loss claims until the return is filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Partnership Information Return (Form CO-17) and Relevé 17 slips for each partner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end (e.g., by June 30 for a December 31 fiscal year-end, aligned with the federal due date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties for late or omitted information returns, generally aligned with the federal CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500; interest and penalties apply to partner balances; the general partner is accountable for the limited partnership's provincial reporting obligations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is required for a Quebec limited partnership under the Income Tax Act or the Civil Code of Quebec; an audit is triggered only by the partnership agreement, a lender covenant, or where the partnership is a reporting issuer for securities-law purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements are prepared under International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE), depending on the partnership agreement and stakeholder requirements; books and records must be kept in English or French, at a place within Canada, and must support the T5013 and CO-17 allocations. The federal and provincial statutory minimum retention period is six years; the seven-year policy in this matrix applies a conservative buffer.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec does not maintain a public beneficial-ownership register for limited partnerships. The annual REQ declaration requires confirmation of the general partners (commandités) and the registered office; the identity of limited partners (commanditaires) remains private. Transfers of partnership interests are recorded internally in the partnership register, and the general partner must file an update declaration with the REQ within 15 days of any change in registry particulars affecting the partnership.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Partnership register of partners (commandités and commanditaires) with capital contributions and transfers
General ledger and accounting records supporting T5013 and CO-17 allocations

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150–370 per year for a commercial registered office and notice-service provider in Quebec, if retained
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 15,000–40,000 per year for a voluntary external audit (not statutorily required); compilation or review engagements typically range from USD 4,000–10,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal corporate income tax rate 15.0% plus Quebec general corporate income tax rate 11.5% = combined 26.5%. A Quebec limited partnership is fiscally transparent; the corporate partner pays Canadian corporation tax on its allocable share of the LP's income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A Canadian-controlled private corporate partner may claim the Small Business Deduction on up to CAD 500,000 of active business income in Canada, lowering the combined rate on that initial tranche to approximately 12.2% (9.0% federal + 3.2% Quebec). No general investment tax holiday is assumed for the zinc die-casting activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CRA Form T5013 Partnership Information Return; filed electronically through CRA Internet File Transfer / approved EFILE service provider. A Quebec LP also issues Relevé 15 (RL-15) via Revenu Québec's CLIC system to Quebec-resident partners.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, based on the partnership's fiscal period.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T5013 must be filed within five months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period. For a calendar December 31 fiscal period, the normal CRA due date is May 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name and business number (BN) of the limited partnership, including the Quebec enterprise registration number (NEQ).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the general partner or any limited partner is non-resident, record the foreign jurisdiction and foreign tax identification number in the partner detail schedule. Do not use a Canadian SIN for a non-resident partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period end date in YYYYMMDD format. Commercial production of die-cast scale automotive models should follow the partnership agreement's fiscal year-end, subject to deemed fiscal period rules under the Income Tax Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners with a treaty PE exemption, confirm that the fiscal period aligns with the home-country reporting period to avoid mismatched foreign tax credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales revenue, partnership business expenses, and capital cost allowance. For a scale automotive die-casting operation, include zinc alloy raw materials, tooling amortization, tampo printing inks, assembly labour, warehouse costs, shipping, and PayPal/Swift transaction fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate only Canadian-source revenue and expenses to the Quebec permanent establishment. Non-resident partners should receive a detailed allocation schedule for use in their home jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of partnership income or loss to each partner, and the limited partner's at-risk amount. Losses of a limited partner are deductible only to the extent of the partner's at-risk amount, adjusted contributions, and recourse debt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate the non-resident limited partner's share of Canadian active business income or loss in Box 32/Box 34 and attach the applicable T5013 Supplementary slip and any NR4 slip for cross-border payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Province or territory of permanent establishment and the business income allocation percentage. If the foundry and tampo line are physically in Quebec, 100% of the partnership's Canadian business income is allocated to Quebec unless another permanent establishment is present.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For treaty purposes, state whether the non-resident partner is carrying on business through a fixed base in Canada. Filing T5013 does not, by itself, create treaty exposure if a PE exemption is available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filed T5013 returns incur a CRA penalty of CAD 25 per partner per day, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500, increasing to CAD 7,500 for partnerships with more than 51 partners. Additional penalties apply for failing to file T5013 slips or for gross negligence, plus statutory interest. Revenu Québec imposes parallel late-filing and daily-penalty provisions.
